top_news.title: Gemini Hacked Three Companies in First Known Breakout by Google’s AI
top_news.dek: Google's Gemini model was used in a security test to gain unauthorized access to three companies.
top_news.brief: In a controlled test conducted by the firm Irregular, Gemini successfully breached three companies. The model gained access by brute-forcing passwords in one instance and by locating credentials in public repositories in the other two. These incidents highlight ongoing concerns regarding the potential for AI models to be weaponized for cyberattacks.
top_news.image_alt: Abstract representation of AI security and unauthorized system access

top_news.title: The last mile of a long road: faster NumPy in the browser
top_news.dek: NumPy in the browser now supports accelerated BLAS via Emscripten-forge, delivering up to 30x performance gains for matrix operations.
top_news.brief: The Emscripten-forge NumPy package now links OpenBLAS in WebAssembly, eliminating the need for slow, loop-based matrix multiplication. Benchmarks at n=1024 show a 30.92x speedup for float32 and 14.90x for float64. Experimental builds with Relaxed SIMD support are also available for further optimization.
top_news.image_alt: Performance comparison chart showing speedup of NumPy matrix operations in WebAssembly

top_news.title: OpenClaw Releases 2026.9.5 With Atomic Updates, Plugin Hot Reload, Conversation Sharing, and Expanded GPT Live
top_news.dek: OpenClaw 2026.9.5 introduces atomic updates to prevent deployment failures and adds plugin hot reloading for personal AI agents.
top_news.brief: The latest OpenClaw release includes atomic updates that validate new versions against a private setup copy before switching. Other features include plugin hot reloading, read-only conversation sharing, and expanded GPT Live integration for meetings. The update incorporates over 4,000 pull requests from the community.
top_news.image_alt: OpenClaw dashboard interface showing new atomic update status

top_news.title: Following OpenAI, Anthropic is also reportedly postponing its IPO
top_news.dek: Anthropic has reportedly delayed its IPO to November 2026 to prioritize strong third-quarter financial reporting.
top_news.brief: Anthropic is pushing back its public listing from October to November 2026. Advisors suggest the delay is intended to showcase robust Q3 results to investors. The company faces scrutiny over high infrastructure costs and ongoing security challenges as it prepares for a potential $2 trillion valuation.
top_news.image_alt: Anthropic logo on a financial news background

primary.title: Linkup Research Releases SPARSEUP: A 149M-Parameter Open-Source Sparse Embedding Model
primary.summary: Linkup Research has released SPARSEUP, an open-source sparse embedding model built on a 149M-parameter ModernBERT backbone. It scores 56.4 nDCG@10 on BEIR-13, which Linkup calls the best result it knows of for a public sparse encoder under 150M parameters. The model uses a logit shift, top-12 expansion per token and case folding to keep its vectors sparse. With the Seismic index, it reaches over 97% recall in about 380 microseconds per query, and it ships under Apache 2.0. The post Linkup Research Releases SPARSEUP: A 149M-Parameter Open-Source Sparse Embedding Model appeared first on MarkTech

primary.title: U.S. military nearly boarded a Chinese ship over a hallucinated AI intelligence report
primary.summary: In the spring of 2026, the U.S. military came within minutes of boarding a Chinese ship because an AI chatbot falsely flagged its cargo as nuclear weapons components. Armed soldiers were ready, aircraft were in the air. The error was caught just before the operation kicked off. The incident plays right into the hands of AI risk advocates who worry less about overpowered AI and more about sloppy systems being used by uncritical or bad-faith operators.
